objectives: Understand business and system state visually within seconds.
Perform routine work through straightforward controls.
Ask Doc for clarification without starting an engineering session.
See what agents are doing, which agent is acting, current phase, exact scope, and why.
Approve consequential changes through clear, exact action cards.
Queue improvements for Claude Code or Codex without supervising the entire build conversation.
Receive verified outcomes, evidence, blockers, and history back in the interface.
Open a heavy Claude Code or Codex session only when exploring, investigating a genuinely complex problem, or constructing something new.

conceptual_roles.The Command Center: business home—what changed, what needs attention, what happens next
conceptual_roles.CARR Control Room: run and observe the system—health, agents, automations, incidents, releases, approvals
conceptual_roles.Claude Code and Codex: exploration, complex investigation, construction, and system improvement

controlling_cutover_test: Can Joe or Dell now complete and understand this routine without opening Claude Code or Codex?
adoption_rule: A feature is not successfully adopted until the controlling cutover test is true for the routine it claims to replace.
retirement_rule: Every displaced session-driven operating ritual has an owner, replacement route, parity evidence, observation window, rollback path, retirement criterion, and retirement event; otherwise the UI is another system to manage.

phase0_baselines.measure: Joe's current weekly time spent using heavy AI sessions for routine system or business operation
phase0_baselines.collection: structured interview plus one representative-week time diary; never infer from token use alone
phase0_baselines.bound_product_action: replace the highest-time routine with a deep-linked visual/control flow
phase0_baselines.post_launch_comparison: same-person weekly minutes on the same routine and measurement window

phase0_baselines.measure: Count and categories of routine questions that require Claude or Codex explanation
phase0_baselines.collection: tag questions during the representative week by surface, intent, and missing explanation
phase0_baselines.bound_product_action: add source-grounded Doc explanation or visible evidence to the owning screen
phase0_baselines.post_launch_comparison: same category counts and percent answered without a heavy session

phase0_baselines.measure: Count and categories of recurring actions that cannot be completed visually
phase0_baselines.collection: interview Joe and Dell and observe a representative week; record exact routine and current workaround
phase0_baselines.bound_product_action: add a typed straightforward control or explicitly keep the routine heavy-session-only
phase0_baselines.post_launch_comparison: same routine inventory and percent safely completed in-product

phase0_baselines.measure: Median time to determine business state and system health
phase0_baselines.collection: timed uncoached tasks from a cold start across representative days
phase0_baselines.bound_product_action: improve Command Center or Control Room overview source, freshness, priority, and deep links
phase0_baselines.post_launch_comparison: same cold-start tasks, operators, and timing method

phase0_baselines.measure: Number of hand-carried context transfers between sessions
phase0_baselines.collection: count manual copy, relay, and return-to-old-task events during the representative week
phase0_baselines.bound_product_action: add durable request context, task-to-task handoff, and verified outcome history
phase0_baselines.post_launch_comparison: same categories and count per week

measurement_gate: No baseline value may be invented. Phase 0 is prepared when instruments/interview prompts and bound actions exist; implementation prioritization requires observed values; post-launch adoption requires a like-for-like comparison.
council_criterion: The frontier-model council—latest qualified Claude, Codex, and Grok models, each at exactly high effort—must reject any roadmap slice that lacks a named routine, baseline plan, bound product action, displacement test, and explicit old-ritual cutover or retention decision.
